title: Draw a brush
summary: Create a solid box brush in a grid view and adjust its size and brush type.
outcome: A selected brush occupies the intended bounds and uses the active material.

sections.title: Create a box

steps.title: Prepare the view
steps.text: Choose the active material in the asset browser, set Grid size, and use the Base and Depth controls for the brush's height through the active grid plane.

steps.title: Clear the selection
steps.text: Activate Create brush (Q), which returns to Select mode. Press Esc until nothing is selected; a selected object makes a normal left-drag move the selection instead of draw a brush.

steps.title: Draw
steps.text: Left-drag in a grid view. The drag sets two dimensions; Base and Depth set the extent through that view. The new box becomes selected.

steps.title: Inspect and resize
steps.text: Frame the selected brush and inspect it in Camera. In Move mode, drag a corner handle in a grid view to resize a single selected box brush, or Undo and draw it again.

sections.caption: A brush can be checked in both a grid view and the Camera.

sections.title: Make a first room

steps.title: Lay a floor
steps.text: In Top view, set a low Base and a shallow Depth, clear the selection, then drag a wide rectangular floor brush.

steps.title: Add walls
steps.text: Raise Base to the top of the floor and set Depth to the desired wall height. Clear the selection before each drag, then draw narrow wall brush footprints around the floor edges. Leave a doorway gap in one wall if you need an entrance.

steps.title: Check the volume
steps.text: Orbit in Camera and use Front or Side view to check that the walls meet the floor at the intended heights. Add a ceiling brush if needed, then save the .map.

tips: For a quick closed shell, draw one box and use Modify > CSG > Hollow. Its wall thickness follows Grid size.

sections.title: Choose a brush type

steps.title: Classify the brush
steps.text: Right-click a selected brush in a grid view and use Brush type for Structural, Detail, Non Collide, Weapon Clip, or Breakable glass as appropriate.

tips: A material changes appearance; brush type changes its editing/build role. Check both before building.
